title: Create Resource
content: Create Resource Lab Resource Go to the AWS Management Console Click Create resource. On the Create page of the selected service: In the Name field, enter: Resource path. Configure the required settings according to your workshop instructions. Click Create resource.

title: Create VPC
content: Create VPC Lab VPC Go to VPC service management console Click Your VPC. Click Create VPC. At the Create VPC page. In the Name tag field, enter Lab VPC. In the IPv4 CIDR field, enter: 10.10.0.0/16. Click Create VPC.

title: Introduction
content:
Session Manager is a function within the AWS Systems Manager (SSM) service. SSM provides secure and auditable instance access without needing to open incoming ports, manage bastion hosts, or handle SSH key distribution.
By using Session Manager, you gain the following advantages over traditional SSH-based methods:
No need to open port 22, increasing security. Can operate within a private network, avoiding exposure to the public internet. Eliminates the need to manage private SSH keys. Centralized access control using AWS IAM. One-click access to instances across platforms. Faster connection compared to traditional SSH. Supports multiple operating systems including Linux, Windows, and macOS. Automatically logs session activity and executed commands. With these benefits, Session Manager can fully replace bastion hosts, saving both time and cost in server access and management.
AWS Services Used in This Workshop: Amazon EC2 – Backend server hosting Amazon SES – Email service for sending notifications Amazon S3 – Static content and asset storage AWS Amplify – Frontend deployment Amazon API Gateway – RESTful API interface Amazon CloudWatch – Monitoring, logs, and metrics

title: Session Management
content:
Server Connection Management for the Restaurant System Overview In this section, you will learn how to manage and maintain connections to the restaurant system’s servers, including both public servers (for customer access) and private servers (for internal use) through AWS Systems Manager - Session Manager.
This feature helps the technical team to:
Securely connect to servers without opening SSH/RDP ports. Monitor and log all administrative activities to ensure security. Manage multiple servers across restaurant branches simultaneously. Contents Feature Introduction Environment Preparation Clean Up Resources

title: Create EC2 Instance
content:
Create an EC2 Instance In this step, we will launch an Amazon EC2 instance and attach the IAM Role created in the previous step.
Go to the EC2 console:
https://console.aws.amazon.com/ec2/
From the dashboard, click Launch instance.
Fill in basic details:
Name: Workshop-EC2 AMI: Choose Amazon Linux 2023 (Free tier eligible). Instance type: t2.micro (Free tier eligible). Under Key pair, select Proceed without a key pair (we will use Session Manager instead of SSH).
In the Network settings, choose your preferred VPC and subnet. Leave security group as default.
Under Advanced details, in IAM instance profile, select SSM-Role (created in step 2.1).
Click Launch instance.
✅ Your EC2 instance will now start and should be visible in the EC2 console.
Make sure the Status check passes before moving to the next step.

title: Create IAM Role
content:
Create IAM Role In this step, we will proceed to create IAM Role. In this IAM Role, the policy AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore will be assigned, this is the policy that allows the EC2 server to communicate with the Session Manager.
Go to IAM service administration interface In the left navigation bar, click Roles. Click Create role. Click AWS service and click EC2. Click Next: Permissions. In the Search box, enter AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and press Enter to search for this policy. Click the policy AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore. Click Next: Tags. Click Next: Review. Name the Role SSM-Role in Role Name Click Create Role . Next, we will make the connection to the EC2 servers we created with Session Manager.

title: Create Method
content:
Create Method for Resource Click Create method (or the equivalent action in the service).
For API Gateway, choose the HTTP method (e.g., GET, POST, PUT, DELETE). Configure required parameters for the method:
Set integration type or runtime configuration. Define request and response formats. Assign any required IAM roles or permissions. Click Create method to complete the method creation.

title: Create Public Subnet
content:
Create Public Subnet Click Subnets. Click Create subnet. At the Create subnet page. In the VPC ID section, click Lab VPC. In the Subnet name field, enter Lab Public Subnet. In the Availability Zone section, select the first Availability zone. In the field IPv4 CIRD block enter 10.10.1.0/24. Scroll to the bottom of the page, click Create subnet.
Click Lab Public Subnet.
Click Actions. Click Edit subnet settings. Click Enable auto-assign public IPv4 address. Click Save. Click Internet Gateways. Click Create internet gateway. At the Create internet gateway page. In the Name tag field, enter Lab IGW. Click Create internet gateway. After successful creation, click Actions. Click Attach to VPC. At the Attach to VPC page. In the Available VPCs section, select Lab VPC. Click Attach internet gateway. Check the successful attaching process as shown below. Next we will create a custom route table to assign to Lab Public Subnet. Click Route Tables. Click Create route table. At the Create route table page. In the Name field, enter Lab Publicrtb. In the VPC section, select Lab VPC. Click Create route table. After creating the route table successfully. Click Edit routes. At the Edit routes page. Click Add route. In the Destination field, enter 0.0.0.0/0 In the Target section, select Internet Gateway and then select Lab IGW. Click Save changes. Click the Subnet associations tab. Click Edit subnet associations to proceed with the associate custom route table we just created in Lab Public Subnet. At the Edit subnet associations page. Click on Lab Public Subnet. Click Save associations. Check that the route table information has been associated with Lab Public Subnet and the internet route information has been pointed to the Internet Gateway as shown below.

title: Preparation
content:
Preparation In this section, you will prepare the necessary AWS resources and configurations before starting the main workshop.
Steps Create IAM Role Create EC2 Instance Create API Gateway Create Amazon CloudWatch Configuration Create AWS Amplify App Create Amazon S3 Bucket Create Amazon SES Configuration

title: Cleanup
content:
Cleanup AWS Resources After completing the workshop, it is important to remove all AWS resources to avoid unnecessary charges.
Steps Delete EC2 Instances
Go to the EC2 Console: https://console.aws.amazon.com/ec2 Select the instances you created and choose Terminate. Delete API Gateway
Go to the API Gateway Console: https://console.aws.amazon.com/apigateway Select your API and choose Delete. Delete Amplify App
Go to the Amplify Console: https://console.aws.amazon.com/amplify Select your app and choose Delete app. Delete S3 Buckets
Go to the S3 Console: https://console.aws.amazon.com/s3 Empty the bucket and then delete it. Delete SES Configuration
Go to the SES Console: https://console.aws.amazon.com/ses Remove verified emails and domains if not needed. Remove IAM Roles and Policies
Go to the IAM Console: https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam Delete any roles or policies created for this workshop. 💡 Tip: Always double-check before deleting resources to ensure you don’t remove anything important.

title: Create API Gateway
content:
Create an API Gateway In this step, you will create an Amazon API Gateway to act as a front door for your backend services.
Go to the API Gateway console:
https://console.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/
Click Create API.
Select REST API and click Build.
In Configure api:
Add name: name-apigateway Click Next, review your settings, then click Create.
Copy the Invoke URL from the API details page — you will use this later to connect the frontend.
💡 Tip: If you want to enable CORS, go to your API settings and enable it for your frontend domain.

title: Create Private Subnet
content: Create Private Subnet Click Subnets. Click Create subnet. At the Create subnet page. In the VPC ID section, click Lab VPC. In the Subnet name field, enter Lab Private Subnet. In the Availability Zone section, select the first Availability zone. In the field IPv4 CIRD block enter 10.10.2.0/24. Scroll to the bottom of the page, click Create subnet. The next step is to create the necessary security groups for the lab.

title: Create CloudWatch Monitoring
content:
Create CloudWatch Monitoring In this step, you will set up Amazon CloudWatch to monitor your application logs and metrics.
Go to the CloudWatch console:
https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/
From the left menu, select Log groups → Create log group.
Log group name: /myapp/backend-logs
Keep default settings and click Create.
(Optional) Create Metrics for custom monitoring:
Go to Metrics → All metrics → Create metric.
Choose namespace and add data points from your application.
Set up Alarms:
Go to Alarms → Create alarm.
Select a metric (e.g., CPUUtilization from EC2).
Set threshold and notification actions.
💡 Tip: You can install the CloudWatch Agent on EC2 to send detailed metrics and custom logs.

title: Create security groups
content:
Create security groups In this step, we will proceed to create the security groups used for our instances. As you can see, these security groups will not need to open traditional ports to ssh like port 22 or remote desktop through port 3389.
Create security group for Linux instance located in public subnet Go to VPC service management console Click Security Group. Click Create security group. In the Security group name field, enter SG Public Linux Instance. In the Description section, enter SG Public Linux Instance. In the VPC section, click the X to reselect the Lab VPC you created for this lab. Keep Outbound rule, drag the mouse to the bottom. Click Create security group. As you can see, the security group we created to use for Linux public instances will not need to open traditional ports to ssh like port 22.
Create a security group for a Windows instance located in a private subnet After successfully creating a security group for the Linux instance located in the public subnet, click the Security Groups link to return to the Security groups list. Click Create security group.
In the Security group name field, enter SG Private Windows Instance.
In the Description section, enter SG Private Windows Instance. In the VPC section, click the X to reselect the Lab VPC you created for this lab. Scroll down. Add Outbound rule to allow TCP 443 connection to 10.10.0.0/16 ( CIDR of Lab VPC we created) Click Create security group. For the Instance in the private subnet, we will connect to the Session Manager endpoint over a TLS encrypted connection, so we need to allow outbound connection from our instance to VPC CIDR through port 443.
Create security group for VPC Endpoint In this step, we will create security group for VPC Endpoint of Session Manager. After successfully creating the security group for the Windows instance in the private subnet, click the Security Groups link to return to the Security groups list. Click Create security group. In the Security group name field, enter SG VPC Endpoint. In the Description section, enter SG VPC Endpoint. In the VPC section, click the X to reselect the Lab VPC you created for this lab. Scroll down. Delete Outbound rule. Add Inbound rule allowing TCP 443 to come from 10.10.0.0/16 ( CIDR of Lab VPC we created ). Click Create security group. So we are done creating the necessary security groups for EC2 instances and VPC Endpoints.

title: Create AWS Amplify Hosting
content:
Create AWS Amplify Hosting In this step, you will deploy and host your frontend application using AWS Amplify.
Go to the AWS Amplify console:
https://console.aws.amazon.com/amplify/
Click Crete new app → Host web app.
Choose your code repository provider (e.g., GitHub, Bitbucket, GitLab, or AWS CodeCommit) and connect your account.
Select your repository and branch to deploy (e.g., main).
Configure build settings:
Framework: React, Vue, Angular, or custom.
Amplify will auto-detect the build command (e.g., npm run build).
Click Save and deploy to start hosting.
Once deployed, Amplify will provide a public URL for your app.
💡 Tip: You can also enable Custom domains in Amplify for your own domain name.

title: Create Public instance
content:
Go to EC2 service management console Click Instances. Click Launch instances. On the Step 1: Choose an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) page. Click Select to select AMI Amazon Linux 2 AMI. On the Step 2: Choose an Instance Type page. Click on Instance type t2.micro. Click Next: Configure Instance Details. At Step 3: Configure Instance Details page In the Network section, select Lab VPC. In the Subnet section, select Lab Public Subnet. In the Auto-assign Public IP section, select Use subnet setting (Enable) Click Next: Add Storage. Click Next: Add Tags to move to the next step. Click Next: Configure Security Group to move to the next step. On page Step 6: Configure Security Group. Select Select an existing security group. Select security group SG Public Linux Instance. Click Review and Launch. The warning dialog box appears because we do not configure the firewall to allow connections to port 22, Click Continue to continue.
At page Step 7: Review Instance Launch.
Click Launch. In the Select an existing key pair or create a new key pair dialog box. Click to select Create a new key pair. In the Key pair name field, enter LabKeypair. Click Download Key Pair and save it to your computer. Click Launch Instances to create EC2 server. Click View Instances to return to the list of EC2 instances.
Click the edit icon under the Name column.
In the Edit Name dialog box, enter Public Linux Instance. Click Save. Next, we will do the same to create an EC2 Instance Windows running in the Private subnet.

title: Create Amazon S3 Bucket
content:
Create Amazon S3 Bucket In this step, you will create an Amazon S3 bucket to store static files or other application data.
Go to the Amazon S3 console:
https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/
Click Create bucket.
Configure bucket settings:
Bucket name: must be globally unique (e.g., my-app-storage-2025).
AWS Region: choose the same region as your application deployment.
For Block Public Access settings, you can keep the default (recommended) or uncheck if you need public file access.
Leave other settings as default and click Create bucket.
Once created, your bucket will appear in the S3 list.
To upload files, click the bucket name → Upload → drag & drop your files.
💡 Tip: You can enable Static website hosting in the bucket properties if you want to serve a frontend directly from S3.

title: Create Private Instance
content:
Go to EC2 service management console Click Instances. Click Launch instances. On the Step 1: Choose an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) page. Drag the mouse down. Click Select to select AMI Microsoft Windows Server 2019 Base. On the Step 2: Choose an Instance Type page. Click on Instance type t2.micro. Click Next: Configure Instance Details. At Step 3: Configure Instance Details page In the Network section, select Lab VPC. In the Subnet section, select Lab Private Subnet. At Auto-assign Public IP select Use subnet setting (Disable) Click Next: Add Storage. Click Next: Add Tags to move to the next step. Click Next: Configure Security Group to move to the next step. On page Step 6: Configure Security Group. Select Select an existing security group. Select security group SG Private Windows Instance. Click Review and Launch. The warning dialog box appears because we do not configure the firewall to allow connections to port 22, Click Continue to continue.
At page Step 7: Review Instance Launch.
Click Launch. In the Select an existing key pair or create a new key pair dialog box. Click Choose an existing key pair. In the Key pair name section, select LabKeypair. Click I acknowledge that I have access to the corresponding private key file, and that without this file, I won’t be able to log into my instance.. Click Launch Instances to create EC2 server. Click View Instances to return to the list of EC2 instances.
Click the edit icon under the Name column.
In the Edit Name dialog box, enter Private Windows Instance. Click Save. Next, we will proceed to create IAM Roles to serve the Session Manager.

title: Create Amazon SES Configuration
content:
Create Amazon SES Configuration In this step, you will configure Amazon Simple Email Service (SES) to send emails from your application.
Go to the Amazon SES console:
https://console.aws.amazon.com/ses/
From the left menu, select Verified identities → click Create identity.
Choose Identity type:
Domain: if you want to send from your own domain (e.g., @example.com).
Email address: if you only need a specific sender address.
Enter the domain name or email address you want to verify.
If using an email address:
SES will send a verification link to your inbox.
Click the link to confirm.
Configure your app to use SES SMTP endpoint or the SES API for sending emails.
💡 Tip: In sandbox mode, SES only allows sending to verified addresses. You can request production access from the SES console.
